question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the 9th Schedule to the Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 4th Constitutional Amendment Act
1st Constitutional Amendment Act
2nd Constitutional Amendment Act
3rd Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1st Constitutional Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 9th Schedule of the Indian Constitution was added by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951. This schedule included laws related to land reforms and farmer welfare to protect them from judicial review. The 1st Amendment amended the Right to Property under Article 31 and introduced Articles 31A and 31B. Laws in the 9th Schedule could not be challenged in courts initially. However, the Supreme Court later ruled that laws in the 9th Schedule are subject to judicial review if they violate fundamental rights, as established in the I.R. Coelho case (2007). This amendment was crucial soon after the Constitution's adoption to safeguard social and economic reforms.

☛ What type of laws are included in the 9th Schedule? → Land reforms and farmer welfare laws
☛ Which articles were added by the 1st Amendment? → Articles 31A and 31B
☛ Which case allowed judicial review of 9th Schedule laws? → I.R. Coelho case (2007)
☛ Which schedule was added by the 1st Amendment? → 9th Schedule
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम ने संविधान में नौवीं अनुसूची जोड़ी गई? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है प्रथम संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की नौवीं अनुसूची को प्रथम संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1951 द्वारा जोड़ा गया। इस अनुसूची में भूमि सुधार और किसान कल्याण से संबंधित कानूनों को शामिल किया गया, ताकि उन्हें न्यायिक समीक्षा से बचाया जा सके। प्रथम संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 31 के तहत संपत्ति के अधिकार में संशोधन किया और अनुच्छेद 31A, 31B जोड़े। नौवीं अनुसूची में शामिल कानूनों को अदालत में चुनौती नहीं दी जा सकती थी। बाद में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने यह स्पष्ट किया कि नौवीं अनुसूची के कानून भी मौलिक अधिकारों के उल्लंघन पर न्यायिक समीक्षा के अधीन हो सकते हैं, जैसा कि I.R. कोहेलो मामले (2007) में कहा गया। यह संशोधन संविधान लागू होने के तुरंत बाद आया, जो सामाजिक और आर्थिक सुधारों को सुरक्षित करने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण था।

question: What does Article 164 of the Indian Constitution state about the appointment of the Chief Minister? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor.
The Chief Minister is elected by the legislative assembly of the state.
The Chief Minister is chosen through a referendum in the state.
The Chief Minister is appointed by the President of India.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor.

Explanation:
Article 164 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister of a state. It states that the Governor shall appoint the Chief Minister. The Chief Minister is the person who, in the opinion of the Governor, can command a majority in the Legislative Assembly. Usually, the Governor appoints the leader of the party that has won the highest number of seats in the state assembly elections. This appointment is not discretionary; the Governor is constitutionally bound to appoint a person who can secure the confidence of the assembly. The Chief Minister holds office during the pleasure of the Governor but is responsible to the Legislative Assembly. The article also empowers the Governor to appoint other ministers on the advice of the Chief Minister.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Basis for appointment → Majority in Legislative Assembly
☛ Governor's role → Appoint CM and administer oath
☛ Relation of Article 164 → State Executive
☛ Tenure of CM → During pleasure of Governor
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 164 मुख्यमंत्री की नियुक्ति के बारे में क्या कहता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 164 राज्य के मुख्यमंत्री की नियुक्ति के प्रावधानों को निर्धारित करता है। इसके अनुसार, राज्यपाल मुख्यमंत्री की नियुक्ति करता है। मुख्यमंत्री वह व्यक्ति होता है जिसे राज्यपाल यह विश्वास हो कि वह विधानसभा में बहुमत का नेतृत्व कर सकता है। आमतौर पर, राज्यपाल उस दल के नेता को मुख्यमंत्री नियुक्त करता है जिसे विधानसभा चुनावों में सबसे अधिक सीटें मिली हों। यह नियुक्ति नाममात्र नहीं है, बल्कि राज्यपाल संवैधानिक रूप से बाध्य है कि वह ऐसे व्यक्ति को नियुक्त करे जो बहुमत का विश्वास प्राप्त कर सके। मुख्यमंत्री का कार्यकाल राज्यपाल के प्रसादपर्यंत होता है, लेकिन वह विधानसभा के प्रति उत्तरदायी होता है।

question: Which of the following conducts the election of state legislatures? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Parliament of India
Election Commission of India
NITI Aayog
State Election Commission of the concerned State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Election Commission of India

Explanation:
According to Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the Election Commission of India has the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, the President, and the Vice-President. It is an independent constitutional body. The State Election Commission only conducts elections for panchayats and municipalities. NITI Aayog and Parliament have no role in conducting elections. The Election Commission ensures free and fair elections.

भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324 के अनुसार, भारत का चुनाव आयोग संसद, राज्य विधानमंडलों, राष्ट्रपति और उपराष्ट्रपति के चुनावों का पर्यवेक्षण, निर्देशन और नियंत्रण करता है। यह एक स्वतंत्र संवैधानिक निकाय है। राज्य चुनाव आयोग केवल पंचायतों और नगरपालिकाओं के चुनाव कराता है। नीति आयोग और संसद का चुनाव कराने से कोई संबंध नहीं है। चुनाव आयोग चुनावों की निष्पक्षता और स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करता है।

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the 10th Schedule to the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 64th Amendment Act
61st Amendment Act
48th Amendment Act
52nd Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 52nd Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 10th Schedule was added to the Indian Constitution by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985, also known as the 'Anti-Defection Law'. This Schedule lays down provisions for disqualification of members of Parliament and state legislatures on grounds of defection, i.e., voluntarily giving up party membership or disobeying the party whip. The amendment also modified Article 102 and Article 191 of the Constitution. Later, the 91st Amendment Act of 2003 further strengthened the anti-defection provisions. The 64th, 61st, and 48th Amendment Acts dealt with other issues.

☛ 10th Schedule deals with → Disqualification of MPs/MLAs
☛ 10th Schedule amended by → 91st Amendment (2003)
☛ Authority to decide defection → Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman)
☛ Prime Minister during 52nd Amendment → Rajiv Gandhi

question: Article 45 (concerning child education) was modified by which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?  (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 73rd Amendment
44th Amendment
42nd Amendment
86th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 86th Amendment

Explanation:
Article 45 originally in the Directive Principles of State Policy directed the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children until the age of 14. The 86th Amendment (2002) made education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A for children aged 6-14. It modified Article 45 to focus on early childhood care and education for children below 6 years. Additionally, it added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k) for parents to provide education opportunities to their children. This amendment was a landmark step towards realizing the goal of universal elementary education in India.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article provides Right to Education? → Article 21A
☛ Which new Fundamental Duty was added by 86th Amendment? → Article 51A(k)
☛ Original Article 45 covered which age group? → 0-14 years
☛ After 86th Amendment, Article 45 covers which age group? → 0-6 years
☛ Which other Article is related to child education? → Article 21A

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts had abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of the princely states?  (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: 44th Amendment Act
36th Amendment Act
26th Amendment Act
42nd Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 26th Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 26th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, enacted in 1971, abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of princely states. It removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Constitution and amended Article 366 to delete the definition of 'princely state'. This amendment was a major step towards social justice and equality, ending the special status and payments given to former rulers. The Bill was introduced as the 31st Constitutional Amendment Bill. The privy purse was an annual sum paid to rulers as a condition for their integration into India.

☛ Year of abolition of privy purse → 1971
☛ Purpose of 26th Amendment → Ending privileges of former rulers

question: Which President of India exercised the pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: R Venkataraman
Zail Singh
Dr. Rajendra Prasad
APJ Abdul Kalam
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Zail Singh

Explanation:
President Zail Singh of India exercised the pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill in 1988. The pocket veto is a power where the President neither signs a bill nor returns it, leaving it pending indefinitely. The bill aimed to increase government control over postal services, including provisions for intercepting letters and telephone tapping. President Zail Singh used the pocket veto as he believed the bill violated civil liberties. This is a notable example in Indian history where the President used discretionary powers to withhold assent. The bill had been passed by Parliament, but the President's inaction prevented it from becoming law.

question: Which of the following talks about 'social and economic justice'? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Fundamental Duty only
Directive Principles of State Policy only
Preamble only
Directive Principles of State Policy and Preamble
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles of State Policy and Preamble

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution mentions securing 'social, economic and political justice' for all citizens. Additionally, the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36-51) direct the state to formulate policies aimed at achieving social and economic justice. Though non-justiciable, these principles are fundamental in governance. For instance, Article 38 directs the state to promote a social order, and Article 39 sets certain policy principles. Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A) focus on citizens' obligations, not justice. Thus, social and economic justice is reflected in both the Preamble and the Directive Principles.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 'सामाजिक और आर्थिक न्याय' के बारे में बात करता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)

केवल राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व

Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व और प्रस्तावना

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना में 'सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनीतिक न्याय' सुनिश्चित करने की बात कही गई है। साथ ही, राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (भाग IV, अनुच्छेद 36-51) राज्य को सामाजिक और आर्थिक न्याय प्राप्त करने के लिए नीतियां बनाने का निर्देश देते हैं। ये तत्व न्यायपालिका द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय नहीं हैं, परंतु देश के शासन में मौलिक हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, अनुच्छेद 38 राज्य को सामाजिक व्यवस्था को सुदृढ़ करने का निर्देश देता है, और अनुच्छेद 39 कुछ नीति सिद्धांतों को निर्धारित करता है। मौलिक कर्तव्य (भाग IV-A) न्याय के बारे में नहीं, बल्कि नागरिकों के कर्तव्यों के बारे में बात करते हैं। इस प्रकार, सामाजिक और आर्थिक न्याय प्रस्तावना और नीति निदेशक तत्वों दोनों में उल्लिखित है।

question: In which case did the Supreme Court introduce the concept of curative petitions? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
Rupa Ashok Hurra vs. Ashok Hurra and Ors.
Indira Nehru Gandhi vs. Shri Raj Narain
M Nagaraj and Ors. vs. Union of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rupa Ashok Hurra vs. Ashok Hurra and Ors.

Explanation:
The Supreme Court introduced the concept of curative petition in the 2002 case of Rupa Ashok Hurra vs. Ashok Hurra and Ors. It is a last resort against a final judgment when all other remedies fail. Derived from the Court's power under Article 137, a curative petition is decided in an open court. To file it, one must prove a gross miscarriage of justice or violation of principles of natural justice. The Kesavananda Bharati case is related to the basic structure doctrine, while Indira Nehru Gandhi vs. Raj Narain pertained to electoral disputes.

question: Who appoints the Chairman and members of the State Administrative Tribunals (SATs)? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: The Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
The Governor of the concerned state
The Prime Minister of India, after consulting the Chief Minister of the state
The President of India, after consultation with the Governor of the concerned state
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India, after consultation with the Governor of the concerned state

Explanation:
The State Administrative Tribunal (SAT) is established under Article 323B of the Constitution. The Chairman and members of SAT are appointed by the President of India after consultation with the Governor of the concerned state. This provision is contained in the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985. The President acts on the recommendation of the central government, but consultation with the Governor is mandatory. This mechanism ensures judicial independence and upholds federal principles. SAT adjudicates service-related disputes at the state level.

question: Fundamental Rights have been provided in the Constitution under which Part? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Part II
Part IV
Part I
Part III
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part III

Explanation:
The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12 to 35) of the Indian Constitution. These rights protect citizens from arbitrary state action. Originally, there were seven fundamental rights, but the 44th Amendment removed the Right to Property (Article 31) from Part III and made it a legal right. Currently, there are six fundamental rights. These rights are justiciable, meaning citizens can directly approach the Supreme Court or High Courts in case of violation. Article 32 provides the constitutional remedy for enforcement of fundamental rights.

☛ Which amendment removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights? → 44th Amendment

☛ How many Fundamental Rights are there currently? → Six
question_hi: मौलिक अधिकार संविधान के किस भाग में दिए गए हैं? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग III (अनुच्छेद 12 से 35) में मौलिक अधिकारों का वर्णन है। ये अधिकार नागरिकों को राज्य के मनमाने हस्तक्षेप से सुरक्षा प्रदान करते हैं। मूलतः सात मौलिक अधिकार थे, लेकिन 44वें संशोधन द्वारा संपत्ति के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 31) को मौलिक अधिकारों से हटाकर कानूनी अधिकार बना दिया गया। वर्तमान में छह मौलिक अधिकार हैं। ये अधिकार न्यायसंगत हैं, अर्थात नागरिक इनके उल्लंघन पर सीधे उच्चतम न्यायालय या उच्च न्यायालय जा सकते हैं। अनुच्छेद 32 मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए संवैधानिक उपचार का अधिकार प्रदान करता है।

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution guarantees 'Equality before the Law' and 'Equal protection of the law'? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 14
Article 19
Article 12
Article 16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 14

Explanation:
Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees 'Equality before the Law' and 'Equal protection of the laws'. It prohibits the State from denying any person equality before the law or equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. This Article falls under Fundamental Rights and ensures equality for all citizens. It is also applicable to foreigners. Article 14 is the foundation of the Right to Equality and any discrimination made under it is considered unconstitutional. It is included in Part III of the Constitution.

question: Who among the following is NOT a part of the Union Cabinet? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Minister of State with independent charge
The Prime Minister
Minister of State without independent charge
Chief Minister of a State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chief Minister of a State

Explanation:
The Union Cabinet is the highest decision-making body of the central government, consisting of the Prime Minister, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State with independent charge, and Ministers of State. The Chief Minister of a State is the head of the state government and is not a member of the Union Cabinet. According to Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution, there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. This Council of Ministers is responsible for the functioning of the central government. Therefore, the Chief Minister is not part of the Union Cabinet.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन संघीय मंत्रिमंडल का भाग नहीं है? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following is a Directive Principle of State Policy mentioned in the Indian Constitution?  (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Constitutional remedies for enforcement of rights of the public
To make provision for freedom of speech
Provision for a uniform civil code
Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Provision for a uniform civil code

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, Articles 36-51. These are non-justiciable but fundamental to governance. Uniform Civil Code (UCC) falls under Article 44, which directs the state to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens throughout India. This is part of DPSP, aiming to replace religious personal laws. Other options like constitutional remedies (Article 32) and freedom of speech (Article 19) are Fundamental Rights, while prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion (Article 15) is also a Fundamental Right. DPSPs are inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to establish socio-economic justice. The UCC remains a significant directive for national integration and gender equality.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भारतीय संविधान में उल्लिखित राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व है? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है समान नागरिक संहिता का प्रावधान

Explanation:
राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (DPSP) भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में अनुच्छेद 36-51 में वर्णित हैं। ये गैर-न्यायिक हैं लेकिन देश के शासन में मौलिक हैं। समान नागरिक संहिता (UCC) अनुच्छेद 44 के अंतर्गत आता है, जो राज्य को निर्देश देता है कि वह पूरे भारत में नागरिकों के लिए एक समान कानून सुनिश्चित करे। यह DPSP का हिस्सा है और इसका उद्देश्य धार्मिक पर्सनल कानूनों को बदलना है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे संवैधानिक उपचार (अनुच्छेद 32) और वाक् स्वतंत्रता (अनुच्छेद 19) मौलिक अधिकार हैं, जबकि धर्म के आधार पर भेदभाव का निषेध (अनुच्छेद 15) भी मौलिक अधिकार है। DPSP आयरलैंड से लिए गए हैं और इनका उद्देश्य सामाजिक-आर्थिक न्याय स्थापित करना है।

question: Which of the following Acts provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Government of India Act, 1909
Government of India Act, 1919
Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1929
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units. This Act aimed to introduce a federal system in India, granting autonomy to provinces and proposing the inclusion of princely states. However, the federation never came into effect because the princely states did not join. The Act included three lists: Federal List, Provincial List, and Concurrent List. It abolished dyarchy at the provincial level and introduced provincial autonomy. At the centre, dyarchy was introduced. It came into force in 1937 and served as the constitutional framework until 1947.

☛ Which system was at the centre in the Government of India Act, 1935? → Dyarchy
☛ When did the Government of India Act, 1935 come into effect? → 1937
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस अधिनियम ने प्रांतों और रियासतों को इकाई मानते हुए एक अखिल भारतीय संघ की स्थापना का प्रावधान किया था? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following freedoms is NOT part of the 'Right to Freedom' under Article 19? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Freedom to form associations
Freedom of conscience
Freedom to assemble peacefully
Freedom to move freely
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Freedom of conscience

Explanation:
Article 19 grants six freedoms: speech and expression, peaceful assembly, forming associations or unions, free movement throughout India, residence and settlement in any part of the country, and practicing any profession, occupation, trade or business. Freedom of conscience falls under Right to Freedom of Religion in Article 25, not under Article 19. The other options (forming associations, assembling peacefully, and moving freely) are explicitly listed under Article 19. Hence, the correct answer is Freedom of conscience.

question: _______ determines the number of the members of State Public Service Commissions. (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Chief Minister of the State
The Governor

solution:

Explanation:
The number of members of the State Public Service Commission is determined by the Governor. question: Who presides over the meetings of the Council of Ministers? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Vice President of India
Prime Minister
President of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prime Minister

Explanation:
According to Article 74 of the Indian Constitution, there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. The Prime Minister presides over the meetings of the Council of Ministers. They allocate portfolios among ministers and ensure coordination of policy decisions. The President is the constitutional head of the state but does not attend these meetings. The Speaker of Lok Sabha and Vice President are also not part of the Council. The Council works on the principle of collective responsibility, and the Prime Minister is its leader.

Explanation:
The Anti-Defection Law was introduced in the Indian Constitution by the 52nd Amendment in 1985. This law aims to prevent elected members from switching parties. Under this law, a member can be disqualified if they voluntarily give up party membership or vote against party directions. The decision is made by the Presiding Officer (Speaker or Chairman). The amendment added the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution, which contains disqualification provisions. The objective of this law is to maintain political stability and curb corrupt practices.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान में दल-बदल विरोधी कानून किस संशोधन द्वारा पेश किया गया था, जिसका उद्देश्य निर्वाचित सदस्यों को पार्टी बदलने से रोकना था? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)

44वाँ संशोधन
61वाँ संशोधन
solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में दल-बदल विरोधी कानून 52वें संशोधन (1985) द्वारा जोड़ा गया। यह कानून निर्वाचित सदस्यों को दल-बदल करने से रोकने के लिए बनाया गया था। इसके तहत, यदि कोई सदस्य स्वेच्छा से अपनी पार्टी की सदस्यता छोड़ता है या पार्टी के निर्देश के विरुद्ध मतदान करता है, तो उसे अयोग्य ठहराया जा सकता है। यह निर्णय सभापति या अध्यक्ष द्वारा लिया जाता है। संशोधन ने संविधान की दसवीं अनुसूची जोड़ी, जिसमें अयोग्यता के प्रावधान हैं। इस कानून का उद्देश्य राजनीतिक स्थिरता बनाए रखना और भ्रष्ट आचरण को रोकना था।

question:
Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts made Sikkim a full-fledged state of India?
  (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: 40th Amendment Act
54th Amendment Act
45th Amendment Act
36th Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 36th Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975 was enacted to make Sikkim a full-fledged state of India. Previously, Sikkim was a protectorate state under Indian suzerainty. This amendment inserted Article 371F into the Constitution, containing special provisions for the state of Sikkim. Sikkim became the 22nd state of India on 26 April 1975.
